input:
Labeled defect
- root cause: the follow-up retry now expands a weak question with the last answered question anywhere in the history instead of the immediately previous turn
- failure path: user asks about landings (answered), then an off-topic question (abstained), then 'tell me more about that'; retrieval is weak, answered[-1] is the landings question, the follow-up is glued to it and the model answers about landings although the previous turn had nothing to expand on

Reviewer finding
- description: The retry now uses the most recent answered question from any earlier turn, even when the immediately previous turn was an abstention. The removed docstring explicitly said a follow-up after an abstention should not get the retry.
- rationale: Trigger: the user asks Q1 (answered), then Q2 about something out of scope (abstained), then a weak follow-up such as 'tell me more about that' that refers back. The old code required the previous turn to be answered, so no retry happened. The new code finds Q1 in the list and glues it to the follow-up, so retrieval uses Q1's topic. The model then answers from context unrelated to the follow-up, which is the outcome the removed docstring warned against.
critique: The finding describes the same mechanism as the label. The retry now takes the last answered question from anywhere in the history rather than the immediately previous turn, so an answered, abstained, follow-up sequence glues Q1 onto the follow-up. Its trigger scenario is the same as the label's.
